text: Yasir Abbas Naqvi ECO MPP (born 25 January 1973) is a Canadian politician who has served as the member of Parliament (MP) for Ottawa Centre since the 2021 federal election, representing the Liberal Party. Before entering federal politics, Naqvi was active in Ontario provincial politics, serving as the first visible-minority attorney general of Ontario from 2016 to 2018, minister of community safety and correctional services from 2014 to 2016, and minister of labour from 2013 to 2014, while representing Ottawa Centre in the Legislative Assembly. He was born and raised in Karachi, Pakistan, and immigrated to Canada after his father was jailed for nine months for leading a pro-democracy demonstration; his family later settled in London, United Kingdom, for a short time. In 1988, at age 15, Naqvi moved to Niagara Falls, Ontario, where his family purchased a motel. He attended McMaster University, earning a degree in Political Science and Life Science, and later studied law at the University of Ottawa, being called to the Bar in Ontario in 2001. He began practicing international trade law at Flavell Kubrick LLP, becoming a partner, before joining Land Michener LLP in 2005 and then serving at the Centre for Trade Policy and Law at Carleton University in 2007. He served as President of the Liberal Party of Ontario from October 2009 to February 2013. The Ottawa Citizen named him one of its "People to Watch in 2010," with a profile in the 9 January 2010 Saturday Observer titled "Yasir Naqvi, he's a firecracker," and Ottawa Life included him in its Tenth Annual "Top 50 People in the Capital" list for 2010. Adam Radwanski of The Globe and Mail called him "possibly the hardest-working constituency MPP in the province" in a September 2011 column. Carleton University recognized him in 2017 as part of its 75 for the 75th series honoring 75 notable alumni in the Faculty of Public Affairs. Prior to politics, he volunteered with community organizations such as the Centretown Community Health Centre and the Ottawa Food Bank. The Ontario Liberal Party opened its nomination in Ottawa Centre in March 2007 after incumbent MPP Richard Patten announced he would not seek re-election; Naqvi competed against Diane Deans and defeated NDP candidate Will Murray by 2,094 votes in the general election. He was re-elected in 2011 and 2014. In October 2007, he was appointed Parliamentary Assistant to Rick Bartolucci, Minister of Community Safety and Correctional Services; in October 2008, to Dwight Duncan, Minister of Revenue; in June 2009, he remained Parliamentary Assistant to John Wilkinson after a cabinet shuffle; and in September 2010, to Leona Dombrowsky, Minister of Education. Naqvi introduced six Private Member's Bills: the "Safer Communities and Neighbourhoods Act," the "City of Ottawa Amendment Act," the "Escaping Domestic Violence Act," the "College and University Student Associations Act," the "Enhancing Red Light Camera System Enforcement Act," and the "Protection of Public Participation Act." Parts of the City of Ottawa Amendment Act were passed in the 2010 budget, and parts of the Escaping Domestic Violence Act were passed in March 2016 under the Sexual Violence and Harassment Action Plan Act. On 17 September 2009, he co-sponsored a proposal with NDP MPP France Gélinas to declare the third week of February "Kindness Week." He also co-sponsored Toby's Act with NDP MPP France Gélinas and PC MPP Christine Elliott, which added gender identity and gender expression to the Ontario Human Rights Code. In March 2013, a Toronto Sun article claimed he had endorsed an Islamist book promoting physical punishment of wives; the next day, in the National Post, Naqvi denied endorsing the book, stating he had written a congratulatory note two years prior but had not read it or authorized its use, and emphasized that he strongly condemned violence against women, calling abuse of any kind unacceptable. In February 2013, when Kathleen Wynne became Premier, she appointed Naqvi as Minister of Labour; after the June 2014 election, he was moved to Minister of Community Safety and Correctional Services and Government House Leader. In 2016, Naqvi and the Ontario government faced criticism over the state of provincial prisons and human rights violations. On 13 June 2016, he became Attorney General, the first visible-minority and first Muslim person to hold the role. As Attorney General, he introduced the Safe Access to Abortion Services Act, 2017, which established safe access zones within 50 meters of abortion clinics and 150 meters of hospitals or healthcare offices providing abortion services, making it illegal to advise against access, videotape or photograph patients or providers, or perform acts of disapproval related to abortion. In a 2018 article, he was named one of the 25 Most Influential in the Justice System and Legal Profession for his Digital Justice Action Plan, which included wireless internet in courtrooms, email and text for jury summons, and a 2017 website for digitizing civil claim filings. Naqvi unsuccessfully sought a fourth mandate in the June 2018 Ontario general election, finishing second to New Democrat Joel Harden. During a brief break from politics, he was appointed CEO of the Institute for Canadian Citizenship (ICC). He was elected as a Liberal MP for Ottawa Centre on 20 September 2021, winning 45.5% of the popular vote, and was appointed Parliamentary Secretary to the President of the King's Privy Council for Canada and Minister of Emergency Preparedness. As a Member of Parliament, he served on the Canadian House of Commons Standing Committee on Justice and Human Rights (JUST) and the Special Joint Committee on the Declaration of Emergency (DEDC). In July 2022, he announced the creation of the Downtown Ottawa Revitalization Task Force to explore recommendations for reimagining downtown Ottawa. He expressed disappointment over the reopening of Wellington Road in front of Parliament, noting that it would bring cars and buses back to the street despite Ottawa's plans for bicycle lanes, and preferred having "conversations" to achieve a better outcome. Naqvi resigned from his role as Parliamentary Secretary in March 2023 to begin seriously considering a run in the 2023 Ontario Liberal Party leadership election, officially announcing his candidacy on 3 June 2023 while remaining a federal MP. He returned to provincial politics in 2023, running for the Ontario Liberal Party leadership while continuing as a federal MP, placing third behind Mississauga mayor Bonnie Crombie, who won, and runner-up Nathaniel Erskine-Smith. Naqvi is married and has a son and a daughter, living in Ottawa. His older brother, Ali Naqvi, ran for the New Democratic Party in Mississauga East—Cooksville in 2015, Etobicoke North in 2008 and 2006, and Don Valley West in 2003. Naqvi's father, Anwar Naqvi, was a New Democratic Party candidate in Halton in 2006 and 2004, and in Oakville in 2003.
